title: The minimum-fort-size conjecture for marginal observances
source: Beth Bjorkman, Sean English and Johnathan Koch, “Cost-Benefit Analysis for PMU Placement in Power Grids”, arXiv:2601.19775 (2026). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19775), Conjecture 4.1

significance.root_decision: The conjecture that minimum fort size at least 4 forces every marginal observance MObs(G;i), for i up to the power domination number, to be at least 4 is false. An explicit graph on 25 vertices, built from two copies of the Fano plane with two lines removed joined through a hub, has no fort of size at most 3, maximum observed-set sizes 11 and 14 with one and two sensors, and power domination number at least 3, so its second marginal observance is 3. (By the referee's computation the maximum observances are 0, 11, 14, 19, 25 and the power domination number is 4.) A generic random search over about 80 million graphs on 10 to 28 vertices found no counterexample; the witness comes from a structured construction.
significance.caveat: No claim that 25 vertices is the smallest counterexample. Lean proves the power domination number is at least 3 (the exact value 4 is the referee's computation). The source is a 2026 arXiv preprint with no citing papers yet. The prior-work paragraph of the paper still refers to internal review files and should be tidied before external use.

root_basis: Root extracted the five modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, axioms exactly the allowed three, no forbidden tokens), and screened the Principia archive (300 ids), the omega registry and GitHub by id. An independent Opus referee compared the Lean definitions word by word with the arXiv and journal texts and the MathDB record, verified the result with its own scripts, read the paper line by line and refreshed the prior-art search.
